title: Non-blocking findings from PR #314's review (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday-followups)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #314 (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday-followups), which accepted the PR. All three items below are quality/robustness observations, not correctness bugs -- none was reproducible as an actual test failure or runtime defect during review.

checklist.step: `tests/unit/data/test_day_trader_intraday.py`'s `test_two_of_three_minute_unit_legs_are_fetched` (asserts `provider.get_hourly_bars.call_count == 2`) and `test_all_three_legs_fetched_for_a_fully_intraday_triple` (asserts `== 3`) now exercise `get_intraday_bars_for_triple`'s genuinely concurrent (`ThreadPoolExecutor`) leg fetching, but still assert on `unittest.mock.Mock.call_count`, whose increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write that can lose updates under real concurrent invocation from separate OS threads (confirmed empirically during this PR's review: 0/20,000 trials mismatched at this test's exact 2-3-calls-per-run scale, but the same harness reliably undercounted `call_count` at high call volume in the same run, while `len(call_args_list)` stayed exact in every trial at every volume tested). The one other test whose assertion became order-dependent under concurrency (`test_non_composable_interval_resamples_from_finest_evenly_dividing_bar_size`) was already updated in this PR to check `call_args_list` membership instead of position -- these two `call_count` assertions should likewise be made robust against the same underlying non-atomicity, e.g. by asserting on `len(provider.get_hourly_bars.call_args_list)` instead of `.call_count`, even though no actual flake has been observed at this test's call volume.

`get_intraday_bars_for_triple` (`backend/app/data/day_trader_intraday.py`, the `with ThreadPoolExecutor(...) as executor: futures = {...}; results = {k: f.result() for k, f in futures.items()}` block) duplicates the same fan-out/fan-in shape already used by `backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py`'s indicator-history endpoint (`with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor: daily_future = executor.submit(...); weekly_future = executor.submit(...)`) -- both hand-roll "submit N independent synchronous calls to a small thread pool, then collect every result" with no shared helper, the same class of duplication this very PR's `resample_ohlcv` extraction fixed for OHLCV resampling. Worth considering a small shared helper (e.g. in a `app.concurrency`-style module) if a third call site appears, though note the two current sites aren't a byte-for-byte match the way the two resample call sites were -- `stocks.py`'s version deliberately resolves futures in a fixed order to preserve a specific error-priority contract (daily-fetch failure takes priority over weekly-fetch failure), which `day_trader_intraday.py`'s version has no equivalent requirement for, so any extraction needs to accommodate that ordering-vs-no-ordering difference rather than assuming the two are identical.

The newly-extracted `app.data.base.resample_ohlcv(frame, rule)` helper has no direct unit test of its own -- it's exercised only indirectly via `StooqProvider._resample_weekly`'s and `day_trader_intraday._resample_to_target`'s existing tests (both of which pass unchanged, confirming behavior-preservation for those two specific rule strings, but not locking down `resample_ohlcv`'s own contract independent of either caller). Worth adding a small direct test module (e.g. `tests/unit/data/test_base.py::TestResampleOhlcv`) covering the aggregation rule and the incomplete-bin-dropped behavior directly, so a future third caller (or a future edit to either existing caller) can't silently break the shared helper's contract without a test catching it at the source.

decisions.decision: Swapped `.call_count` for `len(.call_args_list)` in the two flagged assertions (`test_two_of_three_minute_unit_legs_are_fetched`, `test_all_three_legs_fetched_for_a_fully_intraday_triple`) in `backend/tests/unit/data/test_day_trader_intraday.py`. Verified the underlying claim directly against CPython 3.12's `unittest.mock` source (`CallableMixin._increment_mock_call`): `call_count` is incremented via `self.call_count += 1` (a load/add/store sequence the GIL can interleave across threads, losing updates), while `call_args_list.append(_call)` is a single atomic list append. My own empirical trials (2000 runs at this test's 2-3-call scale, and 2000 calls across 64 threads) didn't reproduce a mismatch on either assertion -- consistent with the reviewer's own note that no flake was observed at this test's call volume either -- but the source-level asymmetry confirms `call_args_list` is the more robust choice regardless, matching the rationale already applied to `test_non_composable_interval_resamples_from_finest_evenly_dividing_bar_size` in the same file.
decisions.rationale: The fix is low-risk and strictly more correct (asserting `len(call_args_list) == N` is equivalent to `call_count == N` when no race occurs, and strictly better when one does), so there was no real alternative to reject here beyond leaving `.call_count` as-is, which the reviewer had already identified as the weaker choice.

decisions.decision: Decided NOT to extract a shared fan-out/fan-in helper for the three ThreadPoolExecutor call sites (`app/api/routers/stocks.py`'s daily/weekly fetch, `app/data/day_trader_intraday.py`'s `_fetch_legs_concurrently`, and `app/api/day_trader_signal.py`'s already-self-shared `_fan_out_per_ticker`, used twice within that module) -- left all three as-is.
decisions.rationale: Re-examined all three sites (the third, `_fan_out_per_ticker`, is the one that appeared since this PR's review, per the checklist item's own prediction). They differ in three ways that make a single shared helper either impossible without new layering or not worth the abstraction: (1) `stocks.py`'s ordering requirement (daily-fetch failure must take priority over weekly-fetch failure) is a load-bearing behavior documented with an inline comment right at the two `.result()` calls -- burying that inside a generic helper's contract makes it a non-obvious invariant a future editor of the helper (working on an unrelated call site) could break without realizing it mattered here; (2) `_fetch_legs_concurrently` lives in `app.data`, which must not depend on `app.api` (the reverse of this codebase's documented dependency direction, docs/architecture/Backend.md), so unifying it with `_fan_out_per_ticker` (currently in `app.api.day_trader_signal`) would require carving out a brand-new shared module (e.g. `app.concurrency`) solely to host a ~6-line `ThreadPoolExecutor`-submit-and-collect pattern, for three call sites whose per-site logic (dedup + capped `max_workers` for the N-ticker case; fixed 3-key dict for the leg case; fixed 2-key ordered case for stocks.py) would still need distinct wrapper functions anyway -- the shared core would save only a few lines of genuinely identical code per site while adding a new module, an extra import per caller, and a fourth place to look when debugging a fan-out issue; (3) unlike the `resample_ohlcv` case this same PR's precedent set (two byte-for-byte identical resample bodies, extracting which removed real duplicated logic with a real shared contract to test), these three sites were never near-duplicates of each other in the way that made `resample_ohlcv` worth extracting -- each already reads clearly at its own call site, and `_fan_out_per_ticker` already unified the two sites that actually were identical (within `app.api.day_trader_signal`). Net: a shared helper here would be abstraction for its own sake, not a genuine duplication fix; leaving the three sites as-is is the better trade-off. This is a legitimate 'not worth unifying' outcome per this task's own description, not a skipped step.

review.notes: Full review of all three items from PR #314's non-blocking findings, all resolved correctly with no blocking issues found. (1) Verified the CPython 3.12 unittest.mock atomicity claim directly against /usr/local/python/3.12.14/lib/python3.12/unittest/mock.py's CallableMixin._increment_mock_call: `self.call_count += 1` is a load/add/store sequence on a plain attribute (interruptible by the GIL across threads, can lose updates), while `self.call_args_list.append(_call)` appends to a `_CallList(list)` subclass that doesn't override `append`, so it's a single atomic C-level list append -- the claim is correct, and the two swapped assertions in test_day_trader_intraday.py are the only remaining `call_count` uses on that concurrently-fetched mock in that file. (2) Hand-verified all four new tests in tests/unit/data/test_base.py against resample_ohlcv's actual implementation (app/data/base.py): manually computed the 10-minute-bin aggregation (open=first/high=max/low=min/close=last/volume=sum) for both bins in the main test, confirmed the single-source-bar-is-kept and empty-frame cases, and confirmed the fully-empty-bin-in-the-middle-is-dropped case against pandas resample's default start_day origin (15:00/15:10/etc. all land on exact 10-minute boundaries from midnight) -- all hand-computed values check out. (3) Read all three ThreadPoolExecutor call sites myself (app/api/routers/stocks.py's daily/weekly fetch, app/data/day_trader_intraday.py's _fetch_legs_concurrently, app/api/day_trader_signal.py's _fan_out_per_ticker) and confirmed both claims underlying the not-worth-extracting decision: stocks.py's fixed daily-then-weekly .result() ordering is a real, commented, load-bearing error-priority contract with no equivalent in the other two sites, and app/data/day_trader_intraday.py (an app.data module) importing anything from app.api.day_trader_signal would indeed invert this codebase's documented dependency direction (docs/architecture/Backend.md's module layout: data/ -> signals/ -> portfolio/ -> api/) -- a shared helper would need a new neutral module for a few lines of genuinely non-identical-enough logic. This is a well-reasoned, non-rationalizing judgment call, properly recorded as a decisions entry. Independently re-ran: backend pytest+coverage (1406 passed, 100% line/branch coverage, no regression), backend ruff/mypy (clean), frontend eslint/tsc (clean, frontend untouched by this PR), scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py (clean), scripts/validate_tasks.py (318 files, no violations). Also ran the code-review skill (medium effort) against the diff independently, which likewise found zero findings. No API route/schema touched (openapi.json check N/A), no new module/dependency/layer added (architecture-review N/A), area is backend/data with skill=null so verify-elder-signal doesn't apply, and this PR has no user-facing UI surface at all (test files + task-board bookkeeping only) so the browser walkthrough (step 9) and persisted e2e suite (step 9a) are both skipped, explicitly, as genuinely inapplicable. No non-blocking findings to track as a follow-up task.

Hand-computed the main test_base.py aggregation case (two 10-minute bins from four 5-minute source rows: open/high/low/close/volume all match the asserted values) plus the empty-middle-bin-dropped case against the actual resample_ohlcv implementation -- both check out.
